problem: Imitation learning needs a new demonstration for every task, while language-only instruction following struggles to convey intricate task details. No prior setting lets an agent reuse a demonstration of a related source task and adapt it using a short language description of the difference.
motivation: Reusing demonstrations with low-effort language reduces the burden of providing demonstrations and could also serve as language-based correction of agent errors. Neither the demonstration nor the description alone determines the target goal, so the agent must combine both modalities, and many adaptations are relational (e.g. 'opposite side of the table').
key_idea: Use a transformer over entity and language tokens to predict the target goal from the source goal plus language (giving a reward), and to adapt source-policy actions to target actions (giving a policy), then combine both to initialize PPO.
insight: Most of the reward-adaptation gap comes from goal prediction rather than the learned distance function (true goal + predicted distance reaches 94.59 normalized on Rearrangement vs 84.19 for predicted goal + true distance). The relational transformer is essential: the non-relational MLP goal predictor nearly collapses (19.76 / 0.11 normalized). Combining policy adaptation (used to initialize the PPO policy) with reward adaptation (used to initialize the value network) beats the oracle-reward PPO baseline and learns faster.
method: Problem setting: given a source demonstration and a language description of the source-to-target difference, learn a target policy zero-shot with no target demonstrations or rewards

Benchmarks: Room Rearrangement (5x5 grid, 2 objects, discrete actions) and Room Navigation (2D continuous arena, 4 objects), each with 3 adaptation types; template language plus AMT paraphrases; 15,000 training datapoints per benchmark

Entity/Language encoders: attribute and noun embeddings plus a linear layer on (x,y) form entity vectors; the language encoder is frozen CLIP, frozen BERT, random-init BERT or GloVe+BiLSTM, with no substantial difference between them

Relational Reward Adaptation: a transformer over source-goal entity tokens and language tokens predicts the target goal (L1 loss); a learned distance d=||psi(s)-psi(s')|| is trained with a pairwise ranking loss; the potential phi=-d(s,g_tgt) gives the reward for PPO

Relational Policy Adaptation: a goal-conditioned behavior-cloning policy predicts source and target actions; a transformer takes the source action, entities and language and outputs the target action, with no RL

Combination: distill the adaptation policy into the PPO actor and the reward-adaptation potential into the PPO critic, keep entropy high (larger std or an entropy penalty), then fine-tune with PPO on the predicted reward

setting.backbone: Small transformer (relational) + MLP; language encoders CLIP (frozen) / BERT / GloVe+LSTM; PPO for RL
setting.training_data: 15,000 synthetic (source demo, language, target demo) triplets per benchmark, with AMT paraphrases for 10% of training points; RL on 30 test tasks
setting.observation: Symbolic entity state (attribute/noun one-hot plus x,y coordinates) and language; no images
setting.action_space: Rearrangement: 7 discrete actions (Up/Down/Left/Right/Grasp/Release/Stop); Navigation: continuous (dx,dy) in [-1,1]^2
setting.simulator: Custom 2D grid / arena environments (Room Rearrangement, Room Navigation)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth entity set and positions are given (no perception); source demonstration is provided

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own custom benchmarks (not standard navigation benchmarks). Reward-adaptation and combined results are counts of successful training episodes during PPO, not SR percentages; the combined approach exceeds the oracle-normalized 100. The text says 5 seeds while the Policy Training paragraph says three RL runs per target task.
results: Reward adaptation reaches about 68% (Rearrangement) and 74% (Navigation) of oracle-reward PPO. Policy adaptation alone gets only 15.33% / 3.87% success with natural language. Combining both, then fine-tuning with PPO, gives 193.44 / 127.75 normalized successes, well above either component alone and above the oracle-reward PPO baseline.
limitations: Only synthetic toy domains with a fixed number of entities and simple template-derived language; no perception or real robot
Assumes ground-truth entity extraction and known entity positions
Goal prediction from natural language remains the bottleneck, and policy adaptation alone is weak
builds_on: Deep RL from human preferences (pairwise ranking loss)
